messages.content: "在一個物理實驗中，你被給予兩個電荷。第一個電荷的大小為5庫倫，第二個電荷的大小為10庫倫。這些電荷相距2公尺。你被要求計算這些電荷之間的電磁力。你進行了兩次實驗。第一次，電荷被放置在真空中，其介電常數為8.854 x 10^-12 F/m。第二次，電荷被放置在一個相對介電常數為5 x 10^-12 F/m的介質中。你能計算出兩種情況下電荷之間的電磁力嗎？"

function.name: electromagnetic_force
function.description: Calculate the electromagnetic force between two charges placed at a certain distance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

charge1.description: The magnitude of the first charge in coulombs.

charge2.description: The magnitude of the second charge in coulombs.

distance.description: The distance between the two charges in meters.

medium_permittivity.description: The relative permittivity of the medium in which the charges are present. Default is 8.854 x 10^-12 F/m (vacuum permittivity). This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Coulomb’s Law**

\[
F=\frac{1}{4\pi \varepsilon}\,\frac{q_1\,q_2}{r^{2}}
\]

where  

* \(q_1 = 5\;\text{C}\)  
* \(q_2 = 10\;\text{C}\)  
* \(r = 2\;\text{m}\)

---

### 1.  In vacuum  

The permittivity of free space is  

\[
\varepsilon_0 = 8.854\times10^{-12}\;\text{F/m}
\]

So

\[
k_{\text{vac}} = \frac{1}{4\pi \varepsilon_0}=8.98755179\times10^{9}\;\text{N·m}^{2}/\text{C}^{2}
\]

\[
F_{\text{vac}} = k_{\text{vac}}\frac{(5)(10)}{2^{2}}
               = 8.98755179\times10^{9}\times\frac{50}{4}
               = 1.12344\times10^{11}\;\text{N}
\]

\[
\boxed{F_{\text{vac}} \approx 1.12\times10^{11}\;\text{N}}
\]

---

### 2.  In a dielectric medium  

The problem statement gives an “absolute” permittivity of the medium as  

\[
\varepsilon_{\text{med}} = 5\times10^{-12}\;\text{F/m}
\]

(If it were meant to be a *relative* permittivity, the absolute value would be \(\varepsilon_{\text{med}} = \varepsilon_0 \times 5 = 4.427\times10^{-11}\;\text{F/m}\); see note below.)

Using the given absolute permittivity:

\[
k_{\text{med}} = \frac{1}{4\pi \varepsilon_{\text{med}}}
                = \frac{1}{4\pi \times 5\times10^{-12}}
                = 1.59154943\times10^{10}\;\text{N·m}^{2}/\text{C}^{2}
\]

\[
F_{\text{med}} = k_{\text{med}}\frac{(5)(10)}{2^{2}}
               = 1.59154943\times10^{10}\times\frac{50}{4}
               = 1.98944\times10^{11}\;\text{N}
\]

\[
\boxed{F_{\text{med}} \approx 1.99\times10^{11}\;\text{N}}
\]

---

#### **Note on Relative Permittivity**

If the medium had a *relative* permittivity \(\kappa = 5\) (dimensionless), its absolute permittivity would be

\[
\varepsilon_{\text{med}} = \kappa\,\varepsilon_0 = 5 \times 8.854\times10^{-12}
                         = 4.427\times10^{-11}\;\text{F/m}
\]

Then

\[
k_{\text{med}} = \frac{1}{4\pi \varepsilon_{\text{med}}}
                = 1.7977\times10^{9}\;\text{N·m}^{2}/\text{C}^{2}
\]

and

\[
F_{\text{med}} = 1.7977\times10^{9}\times\frac{50}{4}
               = 2.2475\times10^{10}\;\text{N}
\]

which is **smaller** than the vacuum force, as expected when the medium has a higher permittivity than free space.

---

**Summary**

| Situation | Force (N) |
|-----------|-----------|
| Vacuum (\(\varepsilon_0 = 8.854\times10^{-12}\;\text{F/m}\)) | \(1.12\times10^{11}\) |
| Dielectric (\(\varepsilon_{\text{med}} = 5\times10^{-12}\;\text{F/m}\)) | \(1.99\times10^{11}\) |

*(If the medium’s permittivity were actually \(\kappa = 5\), the force would be \(2.25\times10^{10}\;\text{N}\).)*
